about: A building's demand by a utility's or a country's own method, one entry for each, read by `building_demand` (building_demand.rs). A building of `n` dwellings asks D = factor·F(n)·d + (factor if `factor_on_common`, else 1)·common + special + commercial + premises, where d is one dwelling's demand: by its floor area (`mean_of: area`, the mean area weighted by the number of each, looked up in `by_area`, each row [up to m², demand], an area between two rows taking the next row up, and `above` the curve coefficient·A^exponent past the last row) or as declared (`mean_of: demand`, the mean of the dwellings' demands, a `grade` naming one, none under `least`). F(n), the `diversity`, is an equivalent number of dwellings, each row [up to n, F], `beyond` what each dwelling past the last row adds. `common` turns the common areas' installed load of a class (kW) into demand by bands of demand factors and a power factor; `premises` the loads other than dwellings by floor area. `entrance` is the supply a demand asks: each row over `over` up to `up_to`, the breaker and the columns as the table prints them. Tables keep the values as printed; `errata` corrects a row the same table in other standards prints otherwise, and `as_printed` uses the printed one. Every table names its source; a test fails on one that does not, on a table out of order and on an erratum that does not match the row. The numbers are the standards', the words are ours. A utility or a country is added as a new entry, never as code.

methods.source: Celesc Distribuição N-321.0003 (revision December 2023, RES. DCL 235/2023), item 5.6.2: DP = k·(F·Da + Di + Dt + Dm) + De + Ds. Equivalents abroad multiply a dwelling's demand by a factor for the number of dwellings in the same way: Spain's ITC-BT-10 (in this file), Germany's DIN 18015-1, France's NF C 14-100, the US NEC 220.84 and the UK's ADMD.

dwelling.source: N-321.0003, Tabela 02 (sheet 66): the demand of one apartment by its floor area, 1.57 kVA up to 70 m²; an area between two rows takes the next row up (the standard's own example takes 91.1 m² as 92 m²)

diversity.source: N-321.0003, Tabela 01 (sheet 65): the diversity factor F, an equivalent number of apartments; it prints none for one apartment

common.source: N-321.0003, item 5.6.2, Di: the common areas' lighting, 100% of the first 10 kW and 25% of the rest, power factor 0.90

Several blocks add the demand of each (item 5.6.1.5).
Special loads (De) count whole, an electric vehicle charging station among them (item 5.7.4); with a load-management system, the demand it manages.

the commercial part, Tabelas 05 to 07 (give it in `commercial`)

methods.source: Cemig ND-5.2 (March 2026), item 7.2: D = D1 + D2, D1 = 1.4·f·a, D2 the condominium and shops by installed load; a least criterion, which another method may replace only with a demand no lower. The tables come from CODI's RTD-027. Equivalents abroad multiply a dwelling's demand by a factor for the number of dwellings in the same way: Spain's ITC-BT-10 (in this file), Germany's DIN 18015-1, France's NF C 14-100, the US NEC 220.84 and the UK's ADMD.

methods.source: Spain's Low Voltage Electrotechnical Regulation (REBT, Real Decreto 842/2002, BOE no. 224 of 18/09/2002), ITC-BT-10, item 3: a building's load is its dwellings' (the mean of their powers × the coefficient of Tabla 1) plus the general services, the shops and offices and the garages, these at a coefficient of 1. The powers are W at 230 V, given here in kW.

dwelling.source: ITC-BT-10, items 2.1 and 2.2: a dwelling's power is the one its owner plans, at least 5.75 kW; the grades basic and elevated

diversity.source: ITC-BT-10, Tabla 1 (item 3.1): the coefficient of simultaneity by the number of dwellings, and 15.3 + (n − 21)·0.5 above 21
